correctness.rationale: For all integer d>=3 and 0<a_i<=1, uniqueness of the scalar water level follows from monotonicity; the centered John ellipsoid follows from symmetry, axial bounds and containment in the ball. The maximal centered axis-parallel contact box follows from strict concavity/KKT. Its complete signed-corner set satisfies the Löwner centered isotropic contact criterion. A direct all-point inequality using the unit ball and coordinate caps proves K is contained in the box Löwner ellipsoid. Sandwiching proves optimality and uniqueness; exact boundary/tie cases, volume ratio and ball criterion follow algebraically. The standalone code was run from the stated artifact and verifies finite examples but does not replace the proof.

value.rationale: The theorem classifies the exact inner and outer optimal-volume ellipsoids for an all-dimensional continuously parameterized model of intersecting a Euclidean ball with independent coordinate capacity constraints. It identifies a surprising exact outer-ellipsoid contact skeleton: the unique volume-maximizing centered axis-parallel feasible box, together with a sorting/water-filling rule and sharp cap-screening thresholds. The exact volume ratio provides quantitative approximation control. This is a motivated complete multi-cap family rather than a one-cut substitution or an arbitrary finite example.
